purpose: Whether the real device photo (R2) costs more to prove than the mirror fixture: eight proves alternating the two inputs in one session, so that drift in the machine's speed affects both alike.
method: One shell loop running c2pa-zk-gnark prove (one process each, in order real, fixture, real, ...) with the same keys; wall time from /usr/bin/time, load_proving_key_s and prove_s from the CLI's own timings. Not run through the benchmark harness: the cache state was not controlled (no eviction; the key files were read by the run before, so likely resident) and not recorded, and peak memory was not measured. Ran right after the harness runs of 2026-11-06-r2-device-photo.json and 2026-11-06-r2-control-fixture.json, on the same machine.

software.note: binaries built from e87ef17; the working tree had uncommitted changes to a document and a test only

real.description: statement inputs prepared from the R2 device photo (pixel10.jpg, sha256 9416d3ea7d2cd815ffdac171d42c254f2dec7cde2c63e9e38d1e9953586b5012) against the official trust list

fixture.description: statement inputs prepared from a mirror-profile fixture (generate-test-pki.sh --mirror, signed with the local TSA)

runs.excluded: wall time 523.4 s against 114.5 s of measured work (load + prove): about 409 s in which the process did not run, a pause of the machine

summary.conclusion: Consistent with similar cost under substantial machine variation: within pairs 2-4 the real input took 3-18% longer, decreasing as the machine's speed settled (pairs 3-4: 5% and 3%). The circuit is fixed-size, so the constraint work is the same; equal wall-clock cost is not demonstrated.
